item.title: Higher properties T and finiteness properties for twin building lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.10101v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Properties $[T_k]$ and finiteness properties $FP_k(\mathbb{Q})$ and $F_k$ are refinements of the following fundamental notions for groups: Kazhdan property T in the first case, and finite generation/presentation in the last two cases. Under suitable hypotheses on the thickness, we prove that every twin building lattice of $(k+1)$-spherical type $(W,S)$, where $k\geq 1$, has property $[T_k]$ and is of type $FP_k(\mathbb{Q})$. If $(W,S)$ is classical, that group is even of type $F_k$. To the best of the author's knowledge, this produces the first examples of infinite finitely presented simple groups with property $[T_k]$ for some $k\geq 2$, and the first examples of finitely presented simple Kazhdan groups that are Frobenius stable and not Frobenius approximable. Along the way, we establish new criteria for property $[T_k]$ for groups acting on CW complexes that extend results of Dymara--Januszkiewicz and Grinbaum-Reizis--Oppenheim. As a key step in our proofs, we determine high acyclicity and, in classical type, high connectivity properties for the opposite complex of a Moufang twin building of $(k+1)$-spherical type and suitable finite thickness.
item.dc:creator: Bianca Marchionna

item.title: Automorphism of reduced finitary power monoids
item.description: arXiv:2611.10645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H$ be a multiplicatively written monoid with identity element $1_H$. The family $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)$ of all finite subsets of $H$ containing $1_H$ is a monoid with identity $\{1_H\}$ under the setwise multiplication induced by $H$. We prove that $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{fin},1}(H)) \cong \operatorname{Aut}(H)$ whenever $H$ satisfies either of the following two conditions: (1) $H$ is commutative, cancellative, and contains an invertible element of infinite order; (2) $H$ is an abelian group which is not isomorphic to the Klein four-group.
item.dc:creator: Yongjie Peng, Guixin Deng

item.title: Marginal Congruences and Elements for Two Commutator Words in Completely Regular Semigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.10680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by Problem 13 posed by Ara\'ujo, Ara\'ujo and Kinyon \cite{Araujo2025} concerning marginal elements, subsemigroups and marginal equivalences associated with commutator words in completely regular semigroups, in this paper we investigate the two commutator words $ \omega_1(x,y)=x^{-1}y^{-1}xy$ and $ \omega_2(x,y)=(yx)^{-1}xy$ on completely regular semigroups. We prove that their marginal equivalences $\sim_{\omega_r}$ ($r=1,2$) coincide and are congruences. More precisely, for a completely regular semigroup $S$, we show that $a\sim_{\omega_r}b$ ($r=1,2$) if and only if $a^0=b^0=p$ and $b^{-1}a\in Z(pSp)$, where $Z(pSp)$ is the center of the monoid $pSp$, and so both words have the same set of marginal elements: \[ M_{\omega}(S) =\bigcup_{p\in E(S)} \bigl(Z(pSp)\cap H_p\bigr), \] where $E(S)$ is the set of idempotents in $S$. We also characterize when this set is a subsemigroup and establish alternative descriptions of the common marginal congruence and marginal elements.
item.dc:creator: Lin Shen, Shoufeng Wang

item.title: A novel Non-Homogeneous Local Representation of the Braid Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.10850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a non-homogeneous local representation of the braid group $B_n$ by tracking the labels of individual strands through successive crossings. Each generator acts through a $2\times2$ block whose position is determined by the crossing and whose coefficients depend on the ordered labels of the participating strands. Starting with the ansatz \[ M_{xy}=\begin{pmatrix}a_x&a_y\\ b_{xy}&c_{xy}\end{pmatrix}, \] for $n\geq3$, the cubic braid relations for arbitrary ordered triples of strands determine $c_{xy}=0$ and $b_{xy}=(1-a_x)/a_x$ in the nondegenerate branch. The moving-label rule leads to an explicit semidirect-product representation, for which we prove the Artin relations and use exact evaluations of the resulting symbolic matrices. In the special homogeneous specialization, where $a_x=a$ for every strand label $x$, the resulting matrix representation is diagonally equivalent to unreduced Burau. We prove that a non-homogeneous specialization of our representation detects Bigelow's explicit nontrivial $B_5$ Burau-kernel commutator. Thus the strand-dependent coefficients distinguish a nontrivial braid that is invisible to the classical Burau representation. This separation provides evidence that the non-homogeneous strand-tracking construction is a promising candidate for a faithful Burau-type representation.
item.dc:creator: Arash Pourkia

item.title: The Herzog--Sch\"onheim Conjecture for Solvable Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Herzog--Sch\"onheim conjecture states that if a group is partitioned into finitely many, and at least two, cosets of subgroups, then two of these subgroups have the same index. We prove the conjecture for all solvable groups, finite or infinite. Sun's bound on unions of cosets, applied in a quotient, is combined with divisibility restrictions on local indices relative to the subgroup generated by the $p$-elements, where $p$ is the largest prime divisor of the order of a minimal counterexample. These restrictions are obtained by counting fixed points in a primitive solvable quotient. This suffices except at the prime $7$, where the counting bound narrowly fails and an additional overlap argument is needed. The proof has been formalized in Lean~4 with mathlib.
item.dc:creator: Murali Menon

item.title: Property $R_\infty$ for Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11294v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every Higman$\unicode{x2013}$Thompson group $G_{n,r}$, with $n\ge2$ and $r\ge1$, has property $R_\infty$. In particular, every automorphism of Thompson's group $V = G_{2,1}$ has infinitely many twisted conjugacy classes. These results answer questions of Olukoya and of Lins de Araujo, de Oliveira-Tosti and Santos Rego. We also prove that a homeomorphism under which no eventually periodic sequence has a finite orbit has a locally finite centralizer in $G_{n,r}$.
item.dc:creator: Ke Wang, Qiang Zhang, Anlan Zhao

item.title: Finite soluble groups with Sylow subgroups of class at most two are IYB-groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every finite soluble group whose Sylow subgroups have nilpotency class at most two is an involutive Yang--Baxter group ($\IYB$-group). This answers a question of Ced\'o and Okni\'nski \cite{CedoOkninski2025}. The main method of the $\IYB$-structures has been reflected in \cite{MengBallesterJimenez2026}.
item.dc:creator: H. Meng, A. Ballester Bolinches, P. Jimenez Seral

item.title: The cohomology of finite simple groups is unbounded
item.description: arXiv:2611.11677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In every fixed positive degree, we show that the cohomology of finite simple groups, algebraic groups and quantum groups, with coefficients in simple modules, can have arbitrarily large dimension. In particular, we disprove Guralnick's conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Chris Bowman, Damian de la Fuente, Nicolas Libedinsky, David Plaza

item.title: Group cosets with all elements automorphically equivalent
item.description: arXiv:2611.11746v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $N$ be a proper non-trivial normal subgroup of $G$. We say that $(G,N)$ is an \textit{automorphically equivalent pair} if for every element $x\in G\setminus N$, the elements in the coset $xN$ belong to the same orbit under the action of ${\rm Aut}(G)$. This generalizes the concept of a Camina pair and constitutes a particular type of equal order pair. In this note, we determine all automorphically equivalent pairs in the class of finite abelian groups.
item.dc:creator: Ryan McCulloch, Marius T\u{a}rn\u{a}uceanu

item.title: Schur multiplier exponents of finite $p$-groups: bounds and critical-class phenomena
item.description: arXiv:2611.11865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Schur exponent conjecture is a long-standing conjecture in group theory, which asserts that $\operatorname{exp}(\mathrm{M}(G))\mid\operatorname{exp}(G)$ for every finite group $G$, where $\mathrm{M}(G)$ denotes the Schur multiplier of $G$. In this article, we prove that the Schur exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups $G$ of nilpotency class at most $2p-2$ when $p$ is an odd prime. Our approach is to establish upper bounds on the exponent of $\gamma_{s+1}(G)$ for $s\in\mathbb{N}$. Using this approach, we further establish exponent bounds for Schur multipliers, nonabelian exterior squares, and tensor squares of $G$ of arbitrary nilpotency class, improving some existing bounds. Moreover, we show that Moravec's Bogomolov multiplier exponent conjecture holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$. Havas conjectured that, for every prime $p>3$, there exists a finite $p$-group of exponent $p$ and nilpotency class $2p-1$ for which the Schur exponent conjecture fails. We show that the Schur exponent conjecture still holds for finite $p$-groups of nilpotency class at most $2p-1$ generated by at most three elements. For four-generator groups of exponent $p$ and class at most $2p-1$, we prove that $\mathrm{M}(G)\cong C_{p^2}^{\,b}\times C_p^{\,a}$ for some $a\ge0$ and $b\in\{0,1\}$.
item.dc:creator: Zugan Xing, Shaowu Zheng

item.title: Extreme amenability and failure of the L\'evy property for the trace-class special unitary group
item.description: arXiv:2611.11944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the trace-class special unitary group, equipped with the trace-norm topology, is extremely amenable but is not a L\'evy group, answering questions posed by Pestov. The failure of the L\'evy property follows from a uniform non-concentration estimate for every nontrivial compact subgroup. Extreme amenability is established through a transverse spectral-gap estimate and trace-norm duality, yielding asymptotic invariance of Lipschitz observables under each fixed finite-dimensional special unitary subgroup. A limiting argument then gives fixed points for continuous actions on arbitrary compact Hausdorff spaces. We also formulate an abstract criterion for extreme amenability based on asymptotic quadratic invariance along a dense chain of compact subgroups. Neither argument uses concentration results for other Schatten exponents.
item.dc:creator: Sergio Luigi Cacciatori, Takashi Shioya, Pietro Ursino, Shigeaki Yokota

item.title: Integrable Measure Equivalence and Gromov's conjecture on nilpotent groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.12009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we prove a well-known conjecture due to M. Gromov that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Quasi-isometric, then their Mal'cev Completions are isomorphic as Lie groups. We prove this result in more general set-up. We prove that if two infinite finitely generated torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent, then the Mal'cev completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Equivalently, using Y. Shalom's result we prove that two infinite countable torsion free nilpotent groups $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are Integrable Measure Equivalent if and only if $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are quasi-isometric if and only if the Mal'cev Completions of $\Gamma$ and $\Lambda$ are isomorphic as Lie groups. Moreover, we discuss some applications of our main theorem to lifting of quasi-isometric embedding from $\Gamma$ to $\Lambda$ to a homo-morphism between their Mal'cev completions, and betti numbers of nilpotent groups.
item.dc:creator: Kajal Das

item.title: Gorenstein modules over Thompson's group
item.description: arXiv:2611.12357v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be any commutative ring of characteristic $0$. We construct an example of a countably presented Gorenstein projective module over the algebra of Thompson's group $F$ with coefficients in $k$, that is not Benson cofibrant. In particular, we provide a negative answer to a conjecture proposed by Dembegioti and Talelli. The construction uses a general method that produces totally acyclic complexes of flat modules and is based on the computation of the (co-)cohomology of $F$ by Brown and Geoghegan.
item.dc:creator: Ioannis Emmanouil, Wei Ren

item.title: Strong pseudo Frobenius numbers
item.description: arXiv:2611.12790v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: By Sylow's theorem, the number of Sylow $p$-subgroups of a finite group is congruent to $1$ modulo $p$, but not every such integer occurs. Frobenius extended the congruence to the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ for every $a\ge0$. Kulakoff and Hall showed that this number is congruent to $1$ or $1+p$ modulo $p^2$ whenever $p^{a+1}$ divides the group order. A positive integer is a Frobenius $p$-number if it is the number of subgroups of order $p^a$ of some finite group for some $a$. There are integers congruent to $1$ modulo $p^2$ which are not Frobenius $p$-numbers, and it remained open whether there are also such integers congruent to $1+p$ modulo $p^2$. We show that no finite group has exactly $106$ subgroups of order $5^a$ for any $a\ge0$.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Sambale

item.title: Restrictions to a principal $A_1$-subgroup
item.description: arXiv:2611.10163v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider simple simply-connected algebraic groups $G$ over the complex numbers, and a principal $A_1$-subgroup $A \leq G$. We show that for most types of $G$ all its irreducible representations $V(\lambda)$ ($\lambda$ a dominant weight) are determined by their restrictions to $A$ up to graph automorphisms. The exceptions are groups $G$ of type $A_l$ with $l \geq 5$ and $G$ of type $D_l$ with $l = 4^m$ and $m \geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Frank L\"ubeck

item.title: Can small transformers learn the language of Coxeter groups?
item.description: arXiv:2611.10936v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The field of mechanistic interpretability is well-suited to collaborative projects between mathematicians and AI researchers. This work describes one such project. We trained a small transformer to learn the language of the Coxeter group affine A2, best known as the symmetries of the tiling of the Euclidean plane by equilateral triangles. We then formulated and proved a word-theoretic conjecture about affine A2 after observing the attention patterns of the trained model.
item.dc:creator: J. Elisenda Grigsby, Yiyao Huang, Arushi Katyal, Ryan Lin, Pranav Ramakrishnan, Weiya Wang

item.title: Twisted pencils of quartics, braid monodromy factorizations, and non-Hopfian Hurwitz curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.11092v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study which groups arise as fundamental groups of complements of affine Hurwitz curves. In every such group the product of the meridians is central and maps to the vector of component degrees in homology; this rules out, for instance, the Baumslag-Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(p,q)$ with $\lvert p\rvert\neq\lvert q\rvert$, and the groups of links with at least two components and vanishing linking numbers. O. V. Kulikova circumvented this obstruction for $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)$ by passing to the non-Hopfian group $\operatorname{BS}(2,3)\times\mathbb{Z}$, which Vik. S. Kulikov's doubling algorithm realizes in degree $768$. We give an explicit braid monodromy factorization of degree 12 with this group. The corresponding curve is not isotopic to an algebraic curve, yet it is obtained from a union of three quartics in a pencil by a single twist along a circle. More generally, for every closed braid $\hat\beta$ we realize $\pi_1(S^3\setminus\hat\beta)\times\mathbb{Z}$ by an explicit Hurwitz curve, again a twist of a union of quartics in a pencil. In the other direction, a Hurwitz curve with group $\operatorname{BS}(k,k+1)\times\mathbb{Z}$ has degree at least $4$, as every Hurwitz curve consisting of a conic and a line is H-isotopic to an algebraic one, after separation of its critical points. Finally, we show that certain semiholomorphic germs, among them those realizing the generalized Borromean rings, are braided surfaces but not Hurwitz curve germs.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Suciu

item.title: Finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.11154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Motivated by the problem of Gragg and Kung on characterizing finite groups with consistent subgroup lattices, we investigate how the consistency of the subgroup lattice $L(G)$ constrains the structure of the underlying finite group $G$. To this end, we first establish several equivalent characterizations of consistency for lattices of finite length in terms of operation-preserving subposets and forbidden sublattices. More interestingly, for complete atomistic lattices of finite length, we introduce the consistency exchange property (CEP) for the canonical closure operator and show that consistency is equivalent to CEP, and that CEP is strictly weaker than the Steinitz-Mac Lane exchange property. We then apply this framework to semidirect products $G=V\rtimes_{\alpha} C_m$, where $V$ is an elementary abelian $p$-group, $m$ is square-free and $p\nmid m$. Writing $d=o(\alpha)$ and letting $C_\alpha=\langle\alpha\rangle$, we prove that $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $d=1$, or $d$ is prime and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pC_\alpha$-module. For prime $d$, this latter condition is equivalent both to the irreducibility of the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $\mathbb F_p$ and to $\mathbb F_p[\alpha]$ being a field. More generally, we verify that if $G=V\rtimes_\theta H$ where $H$ acts faithfully on $V$ and $p\nmid |H|$, then $L(G)$ is consistent if and only if either $H$ is trivial, or $H$ is cyclic of prime order and $V$ is isotypic as an $\mathbb F_pH$-module. We thus obtain a complete solution to the problem of Gragg and Kung for this class of coprime semidirect products.
item.dc:creator: Peng He, Xue-ping Wang

item.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.11184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.
item.dc:creator: Xiaojun Wu

item.title: On Proximity Subgroups of Groups
item.description:
arXiv:2611.11185v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By a $	extit{proximity subgroup}$ of a group $G$ we mean a norm $
u$ on $G$ valued in a complete lattice $L$ equipped with a binary sum (an additive counterpart of a multiplicative structure). The idea is that the smaller the value $
u(y)$ is, the closer $y\in G$ is to the subgroup of $G$ defined by the equation $
u(x)= ot$, where $ ot$ is the bottom element of $L$. We test whether this notion is a suitable substitute for the usual notion of a subgroup (recovered by taking $L=\{ ot,	op\}$ with join as the sum), by showing that the form of proximity subgroups is noetherian. Intuitively, this means that proximity subgroups are as well suited for formulating and proving isomorphism theorems and homological diagram lemmas for groups as the usual subgroups are. We study several questions in relation to this, including what makes the noetherian form of usual subgroups special among all of these noetherian forms, and in fact, all noetherian forms of the category of groups.
item.dc:creator: Kishan Dayaram, Zurab Janelidze, Ronald Kerario

item.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.11195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact K\"ahler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Liu

item.title: On the monotonicity of amenable category for geometric 4-manifolds and their connected sums
item.description: arXiv:2611.11247v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the amenable category is monotone with respect to the domination relation for geometric $4$-manifolds and their connected sums.
item.dc:creator: Pietro Capovilla, Alberto Casali, Christoforos Neofytidis

item.title: Fundamental Groups of Permutation Complexes
item.description: arXiv:2611.11362v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an elementary argument showing that fundamental groups of permutation complexes are free. Hence, $\mathbb{R} P^2$ cannot be realized by a permutation complex, answering a question of Chach\'olski, Levi and Meshulam.
item.dc:creator: Dejan Govc

item.title: Sections of the Kottwitz homomorphism and affine pinnings
item.description: arXiv:2611.11363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected reductive group split over $\mathbb{Z}$. The Kottwitz homomorphism identifies the group of connected components of the loop group of $G$ with the group $\Omega$ of length zero elements of the extended affine Weyl group. We show that this homomorphism always has a homomorphic section, and that the section can be chosen inside the normalizer of $T$ in $G(\mathbb{Z}[t,t^{-1}])$. We then ask whether the section can be chosen to preserve an affine pinning. This is possible if no simple factor of $G$ is of type $B_{2m}$ or $C_{2m}$. It is impossible for $(SL_2\times Sp_{2n})/\mu_2$ and $(SL_2\times Spin_{2n+1})/\mu_2$ when $n$ is even. We show that the obstructions for $G$ and for its Langlands dual group are dual to each other, and we compute them by a lattice computation with a Coxeter element. As an application, we show that the component group of the centralizer of any semisimple element lifts to the centralizer. Under the same condition on the simple factors, the lift can be chosen to preserve a pinning of the neutral component.
item.dc:creator: Yau Wing Li

item.title: Dualities and completions of median algebras and semilattices: a universal-algebraic approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.12469v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that universal algebra, and the theory of natural dualities in particular, provides a uniform framework for the dualities between median algebras and bounded poc sets and their Boolean topological variants. We identify the Roller compactification of a CAT(0) cube complex with the profinite completion and the natural extension of the median algebra of its vertices. We then develop the order-theoretic perspective, which leads to a characterization of the profinite completion by the property that its intervals are the canonical extensions of the original ones. Since the basepoint orders of a median algebra have no top in general, we introduce conditional canonical extensions, show that they are unique, and realize them inside the profinite completion. Finally, a transfer theorem carries universal sentences from the finite quotients of a median algebra to its profinite completion, and we close with open questions on a correspondence theory between median algebras and their bounded poc sets.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Teheux

item.title: Lie algebras graded by the root system $AG_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study Lie algebras graded by the generalized root system $AG_2$, which is obtained from $G_2$ by adjoining the doubles of its short roots, over fields of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$. We show that every such Lie algebra with a grading subalgebra of type $A_2$ is, modulo its center, the Tits-Kantor-Koecher Lie algebra of a structurable algebra equipped with an idempotent $t$ satisfying $t+\overline{t}=1$. Conversely, every structurable algebra with such an idempotent gives rise to an $(AG_2,A_2)$-graded Lie algebra. We describe the corresponding Peirce decomposition and characterize the additional algebraic structure required for an $(AG_2,G_2)$-grading. Using the classification of central simple structurable algebras, we determine the central simple examples when the characteristic is also different from $5$. Finally, we compare our constructions with the theory of Tits hexagons. For the central simple examples in which all root spaces are non-zero, we determine which ones are Tits-hexagonalizable; in certain cases, this imposes an additional balancing condition on the idempotent.
item.dc:creator: Tom De Medts, Michiel Smet

item.title: Doubly Sequenceable Groups
item.description: arXiv:2208.14334v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a sequence ${\bf g}: g_0,\dots,g_m$ in a finite group $G$ with $g_0=1_G$, let $\bar{\bf g}:\bar g_0,\dots,\bar g_m$ be the sequence of consecutive quotients of $\bf g$, defined by $\bar g_0=1_G$ and $\bar g_i=g_{i-1}^{-1}g_i$ for $1\le i\le m$. We say that $G$ is \emph{doubly sequenceable} if there exists a sequence $\bf g$ in $G$ such that every element of $G$ appears exactly twice in each of $\bf g$ and $\bar{\bf g}$; such a sequence is \emph{cyclic} if its last term is $1_G$. We show that every group that is abelian, of odd order, sequenceable, R-sequenceable, or terraced has a cyclic double sequencing, and that a group is terraced if and only if it has a palindromic cyclic double sequencing. We show that if $H$ is a group of odd order or a sequenceable group and $K$ is an abelian group, then $H\times K$ has a cyclic double sequencing. We also show that if $H$ has a cyclic double sequencing and $K$ is an abelian group with no direct summand of order $2$, then $H\times K$ has a cyclic double sequencing, and we extend this to terraced groups $H$ and abelian groups $K$ with at most six direct summands of order $2$. Consequently, complete double Latin squares exist for every order, and the double sequencing conjecture holds for all groups of order at most $87$ except possibly $64$, and for all sufficiently large groups.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Doubly sequenceable groups, J. Combin. Designs 32 (2024), no. 7, 371-387
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: The multiples of a numerical semigroup
item.description: arXiv:2402.04413v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given two numerical semigroups $S$ and $T$ we say that $T$ is a multiple of $S$ if there exists an integer $d \in \mathbb{N} \setminus \{0\}$ such that $S = \{x \in \mathbb{N} \mid d x \in T\}$. In this paper we study the family of multiples of a (fixed) numerical semigroup. We also address the open problem of finding numerical semigroups of embedding dimension $e$ without any quotient of embedding dimension less than $e$, and provide new families with this property.
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Ojeda, Jos\'e Carlos Rosales

item.title: Subgroup Separability of Artin Groups II
item.description: arXiv:2403.05483v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this short note, we establish a more concrete characterization of subgroup separable (LERF) Artin groups, building on a previously known criterion. Specifically, we prove an Artin group is LERF if and only if its underlying graph does not contain certain induced subgraphs, thus providing a more direct generalization of the Metaftsis-Raptis criterion for RAAGs. Consequently, we prove every LERF Artin group is coherent and obtain a graph condition for coherent Artin groups to be LERF.
item.dc:creator: Kisnney Almeida, Igor Lima

item.title: Some invariants of totally disconnected locally compact groups: cohomology and combinatorics
item.description: arXiv:2408.15716v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The paper investigates two invariants for totally disconnected locally compact (t.d.l.c.) groups: the number of ends and the rational discrete cohomological dimension. Firstly, for a compactly generated t.d.l.c. group $G$, it is shown that its number of ends can be expressed in terms of the low-dimensional rational discrete cohomology of $G$, generalising a notable theorem by E. Specker to the t.d.l.c. setting. Secondly, we focus on a t.d.l.c. group $G$ acting under suitable conditions on a building $\Delta$, showing that both the number of ends and the rational cohomological dimension of $G$ are related to those of the Weyl group associated to $\Delta$. In special cases, we compare the rational discrete cohomological dimension of $G$ to its flat-rank, and in the appendix we provide examples for which these two invariants coincide. Finally, for t.d.l.c. groups with rational discrete cohomological dimension one that act properly and chamber-transitively on locally finite buildings, we explicitly construct a proper cocompact action on a tree out of the action on the building. All the results of independent interest in Coxeter theory have been included in the appendix.
item.dc:creator: Ilaria Castellano, Bianca Marchionna, Thomas Weigel

item.title: Symmetric harmoniousness of odd-order groups
item.description: arXiv:2511.13430v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every group of odd order is symmetric harmonious, i.e., there exists a permutation $g_0,g_1,\dots,g_{\ell-1}$ of the elements of $G$ such that the consecutive products $g_0g_1,g_1g_2,\dots,g_{\ell-1}g_0$ also form a permutation of the elements of $G$ and $g_{\ell-i}=g_i^{-1}$ for all $1\le i\le \ell-1$, where $\ell=|G|$. Consequently, a group is symmetric harmonious if and only if it has odd order. We also characterize symmetric harmonious sequences in terms of complete mappings. As applications we obtain new examples of R*-sequenceable groups, and we show that every split extension of an odd-order group by a harmoniously matched group is both harmonious and \#-harmonious. Together with several new harmoniously matched groups ($D_{12},D_{16},D_{20},D_{24},Q_{16},Q_{24},A_4,S_4$), this yields many non-abelian groups that are both harmonious and \#-harmonious, including infinite families of dihedral and dicyclic groups and all $2$-nilpotent groups with an abelian Sylow $2$-subgroup that is neither cyclic nor elementary abelian and is central in its normalizer.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Symmetric harmoniousness of odd-order groups, Austral. J Combin. 96 (2026), no. 1, 134-141
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: More Residually Solvable One-Relator Groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.13933v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We say a word in a free group is ``partially positive'' if there is at least one generator which appears in the word, but does not appear with negative exponent. We show that one-relator groups with a partially positive relator are residually solvable. This extends a theorem of Baumslag showing one-relator groups with positive relators are residually solvable.
item.dc:creator: Lucy Koch-Hyde, Siobhan O'Connor, Eamonn Olive

item.title: Character Nonvanishing under Coprime Actions
item.description: arXiv:2609.16227v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let a finite group $A$ act coprimely on a finite group $G$, and let $C=C_G(A)$. Navarro asked whether an $A$-invariant irreducible character has linear Glauberman--Isaacs correspondent if and only if it is nonvanishing on $C$. We give counterexamples to this equivalence. We also prove that when $G$ is nilpotent, nonvanishing on $C$ implies that the Glauberman--Isaacs correspondent is linear.
item.dc:creator: Eric Hou

item.title: A proof of the sharpness conjectures for all saturated fusion systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.02043v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the D\'iaz$\unicode[Arial]{x2013}$Park conjecture for sharpness of saturated fusion systems. More generally, for every saturated fusion system $\mathcal F$ over a finite $p$-group and every Mackey functor for $\mathcal F$ over the localisation $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$ of the integers at $p$, the higher limits of its contravariant part over the centric orbit category vanish in all positive degrees. In particular, the subgroup and normaliser decompositions of every $p$-local finite group $(S,\mathcal F,\mathcal L)$ over the $\mathcal F$-centric subgroups are sharp. This answers in the affirmative a question in the list of important open problems in [M. Aschbacher, R. Kessar and B. Oliver, Fusion Systems in Algebra and Topology, Cambridge Univ. Press (2011)], and proves the sharpness conjecture stated in [M. Aschbacher and B. Oliver, Fusion systems, Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (2016)] and Conjecture 1.2 of [E. Yal\c{c}$\unicode[Arial]{x131}$n, Higher limits over the fusion orbit category, Adv. Math. (2022)]. The proof is algebraic and does not rely on the classification of finite simple groups.
item.dc:creator: Baoyu Zhang, Shengmin Zhang

item.title: Alperin weight bijections and dimensions of simple modules
item.description: arXiv:2611.05271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a new refinement of the (blockwise) Alperin weight conjecture taking dimensions of simple modules (or degrees of irreducible Brauer characters) into consideration. This is similar to Giannelli's refinement of the (Alperin--)McKay conjecture. We prove this new refinement for blocks with a cyclic or Klein four defect group, for inertial blocks (which include the Brou\'{e}--Puig nilpotent blocks), and for $p$-blocks of $p$-solvable groups.
item.dc:creator: Xin Huang, Hanxiao Li

item.title: On rational representations and rational group algebra of $\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$
item.description: arXiv:2606.02415v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we study rational representations of $G=\operatorname{GL}_2(q)$, where $q$ is a prime power. Let $\rho$ be an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then $\rho$ affords the character \[ \Omega(\chi)=m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)\sum_{\sigma\in\operatorname{Gal}(\mathbb{Q}(\chi)/\mathbb{Q})}\chi^{\sigma}, \] for some irreducible complex character $\chi$ of $G$, where $m_{\mathbb{Q}}(\chi)$ denotes the Schur index of $\chi$ over $\mathbb{Q}$, and conversely, every character of this form is afforded by an irreducible representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Q}$. We obtain a combinatorial description for the counting of inequivalent irreducible $\mathbb{Q}$-representations of $G$ of each distinct degree. Furthermore, we briefly determine the rational character table of $G$ and present a method for constructing an irreducible rational matrix representation $\rho$ of $G$ affording the character $\Omega(\chi)$, where $\chi$ is an irreducible complex character of $G$ arising from parabolic induction. Finally, using the results on the rational representations of $G$, we derive an explicit combinatorial formula, depending only on $q$, for the Wedderburn decomposition of $\mathbb{Q}G$.
item.dc:creator: Ram Karan Choudhary, Sunil Kumar Prajapati

item.title: A uniform decomposition theorem for invariant differential operators on imprimitive complex reflection groups G(r,p,n)
item.description: arXiv:2608.01474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: {We study the module structure of the polynomial ring, localized at the discriminant, over the ring of differential operators on the ring of invariants of the imprimitive complex reflection group $G(r,p,n)$, describing its simple components with explicit generators given by the higher Specht polynomials of Ariki--Terasoma--Yamada. The proof rests on a Jacobian lemma computing the discriminant of $G(r,p,n)$, combined with a double-centralizer argument. As particular cases ($r=2$, $p=2$ or $p=1$) we recover, and considerably shorten, the known decomposition theorems for the real reflection groups $W(D_n)$ and $W(B_n)$; we also treat $G(r,r,n)$ and $G(r,1,n)$ explicitly, with worked examples ($D_2$, $D_3$, $B_2$) and their central idempotents. Finally, applying the Galois descent equivalence of categories of Nonkan\'e to $G(r,p,n)$ for the first time gives a second, generator-free description of the simple summands as twisted invariants.}
item.dc:creator: Jean Kabor\'e, Ibrahim Nonkan\'e

item.title: Profinite Non-Rigidity of Arithmetic Lattices and the K\"ahler Property
item.description: arXiv:2609.31523v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the K\"ahlerness of a finitely presented, residually finite group is not determined by its profinite completion, which answers a question asked independently by Arapura and Libgober. In the proof, we give explicit constructions to characterize the absolute Dynkin types that admit non-isomorphic real forms of higher-rank Lie groups containing torsion-free arithmetic lattices with isomorphic profinite completions.
item.dc:creator: Yukun Du, Feng Hao, Kejia Zhu

item.title: Arbitrary Stage Spectra for Raikov Remainders Along Quotient Towers
item.description: arXiv:2610.02212v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\theta$ be an ordinal and let $(N_\alpha)_{\alpha\leq\theta}$ be a continuous increasing tower of closed normal subgroups of a Hausdorff topological group $G$, with $N_0=\{e\}$. Write $\rho G$ for the Raikov completion of $G$, and put $K_\alpha=\overline{N_\alpha}^{\rho G}$ and $H_\alpha=GK_\alpha$. The successive and limit differences of the groups $H_\alpha$ mark the first stages at which points of $\rho G$ become old quotient points. For every nonzero ordinal $\theta$ and every set $S\subseteq(0,\theta]$, there is a Hausdorff pseudocompact Boolean group with a continuous tower of closed normal subgroups such that every member of the tower is pseudocompact and the nonempty strata occur exactly at the stages in $S$. The terminal quotient can simultaneously be chosen isomorphic to $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$, and for every $\delta<\theta$ the successive factor $N_{\delta+1}/N_\delta$ is compact exactly when $\delta+1\notin S$. Thus a tower may have a single nonempty stratum at a limit stage even when every successive factor is compact. For a closed normal subgroup $N$ of $G$, let $\widehat q:\rho G\to\rho(G/N)$ extend the quotient homomorphism and put $K=\overline N^{\rho G}$. Over $gN\in G/N$, the fiber in $\rho G\setminus G$ is $g(K\setminus N)$, homeomorphic to $\rho N\setminus N$, while for $y\in\widehat q(\rho G)\setminus(G/N)$ the entire $\widehat q$-fiber lies in $\rho G\setminus G$ and is homeomorphic to $\rho N$. For precompact kernels this gives a canonical decomposition, and nested quotients give the two-stage identity underlying the transfinite filtration. Further results concern pseudocompact Raikov remainders and include countable Abelian examples.
item.dc:creator: Xing-Yu Hu

item.title: Discontinuous actions of rational special linear groups on manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.15653v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every $n\geq 1$, we construct continuum-many pairwise non-conjugate actions of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{Q})$ by homeomorphisms on the $n$-sphere. None of these actions extend to a continuous action of $\operatorname{SL}(n+1,\mathbb{R})$. Our construction refines a blow-up procedure of Bowden and Mann, allowing the stabiliser action inside each blown-up disc to be prescribed. We motivate studying these actions and record some related observations.
item.dc:creator: Segev Gonen Cohen

item.title: Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters
item.description: arXiv:2610.37291v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. Such a geometric realization enables the construction of canonical bases, integral forms, and monoidal categorification for these unequal-parameter iSchur algebras and the corresponding iquantum groups. This material is not a formal generalization from the equal-parameter case to the unequal-parameter case. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. For example, the support varieties of generators of an integral form may not be rationally smooth, the categorification is provided by the category of descent data of semisimple complexes fixed by the twisted Frobenius, and the positivity of the canonical basis is established using a refined covering.
item.dc:creator: Li Luo, Rui Song, Yang Yang
